A full‑time employee with three years of service accrues **20 days of PTO per calendar year** (160 hours).  
This is set out in the Paid Time Off policy: POL‑PTO‑001 §2.1 Accrual Rates.

Helios observes a set of paid holidays that differ by office location.

* **United States offices** – 12 paid holidays (e.g., New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, etc.) (POL‑HOL‑001 §2.1).  
* **Singapore (APAC) office** – 11 paid holidays (e.g., Chinese New Year, Good Friday, Hari Raya Puasa, etc.) (POL‑HOL‑001 §2.3).

Because the policy specifies that employees “observe the holiday schedule of their **assigned office location**” (POL‑HOL‑001 §5), the holiday count is **not the same in every office**. Employees in other regions would follow the schedule listed for their own location.

You may work from another country for **up to 30 calendar days in a rolling 12‑month period** (across all countries combined).  In addition, each eligible country has its own maximum consecutive‑day limit (e.g., 21 days in Spain, Italy, Germany, etc., and 30 days in Ireland, Portugal, UK, etc.) (POL‑INTL‑001 §2 The 30‑Day Rule).

**Answer**

- **Domestic hotel cap:** $200 per night (unless the city is a Tier 1 city—New York or San Francisco—then the cap is $300).  
- **Receipts required:** An itemised receipt for every expense of $25 or more. The receipt must show the vendor, date, itemised amounts, and total. Credit‑card statements alone are not acceptable.

**Citations**

- POL‑EXP‑001 §4 Lodging – “Reimbursable up to $300 per night in Tier 1 cities … and $200 per night elsewhere, excluding taxes and mandatory fees.”  
- POL‑EXP‑001 §2.2 Receipts – “An itemised receipt is required for every expense of $25 or more… Receipts must show the vendor, date, itemised amounts, and total.”

Report the theft to the Security Operations Center **immediately**—and in any case **within 4 hours** of discovering the loss.  
Send an email to `security@helios.example.com` or call +1‑555‑0100. Late reporting is itself a policy violation. (POL‑SEC‑001 §3.3 Lost or Stolen Devices)

The PTO policy's blackout-period rule is in **POL-PTO-001 §4 Blackout Periods** (v4.1, effective 2026-01-01). It reads:

> "To protect delivery and customer commitments, the following are blackout periods during which PTO requests of **3 or more consecutive days** are generally denied:
>
> - **Fiscal close:** the last 5 business days and first 3 business days of each fiscal quarter (fiscal quarters end March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31).
> - **Annual customer conference:** the week of the Helios Forum conference (September 14 – 18, 2026).
> - **Peak support season (Customer Support org only):** November 15 – January 5.
>
> Exceptions to a blackout period require VP-level approval. Blackout periods do not apply to statutory leave under `POL-LEAVE-002`, to bereavement leave, or to jury duty."

Key points:
- Only requests of **3+ consecutive days** are affected — shorter requests are not blocked by a blackout.
- The blackout is a "generally denied" rule, not an absolute ban: **VP-level approval** can grant an exception.
- Exempt from blackouts: statutory leave (POL-LEAVE-002), bereavement leave, and jury duty.

Note the fiscal-close window is currently relevant: fiscal Q3 ends September 30, 2026, so the last 5 business days before that (and first 3 after) are a blackout.

1. **Insufficient balance** — Jonas has **13 hours (1.62 days)** of PTO available, but the request is for **24 hours (3 days)** — a shortfall of **11 hours** (POL-PTO-001 §3.3 Insufficient Balance).

2. **Insufficient notice** — 21 Sep is **6 business days** from today (12 Sep), but 3 consecutive business days of PTO requires **10 business days** notice (POL-PTO-001 §3.1 Notice Requirements).

- **Move the start date later** so that 10 business days' notice is met. For 3 consecutive business days, the earliest compliant start would be **29 September 2026** (10 business days after 12 Sep) — but even then, the balance shortfall still blocks a full 3-day request.

Tomas Silva (E-1120, Data Scientist, Austin, H-1B) needs to **submit an International Remote Work request in Helios Workday at least 20 business days before the intended start date**, specifying Brazil, exact dates, and total calendar days. That submission is the first step — nothing else can proceed until it's filed.

Because he's on an H-1B, the request will also need **Immigration Counsel clearance** (step 4 of the workflow), since travel may affect his status or re-entry.

The full approval chain after submission:
1. **Manager approval** (David Okafor) — coverage and time-zone overlap (POL-INTL-001 §4 Approval Workflow)
2. **Global Mobility & Tax review** — confirms Brazil is eligible and the day count is within limits
3. **Immigration check** — H-1B holders require additional Immigration Counsel clearance
4. **Information Security review** — required for all international requests
5. **Written approval issued in Workday** — no travel should be booked before this

Typical end-to-end approval time is 10–20 business days. Requests submitted with less than 20 business days' notice are reviewed on a best-effort basis and frequently denied for lack of review time (POL-INTL-001 §4 Approval Workflow).

**Bottom line:** Tomas should file the Workday request now, with exact dates, to give the full approval chain time to complete before his intended start date.

**Yes — that window falls inside the fiscal-close blackout period.**

The fiscal-close blackout covers the last 5 business days and first 3 business days of each fiscal quarter, with quarters ending December 31 (POL-PTO-001 §4 Blackout Periods). Since the Q4 fiscal quarter ends 31 December 2026:

- **28 Dec 2026 (Tue) – 31 Dec 2026 (Fri)** — the last 5 business days of the quarter (28, 29, 30, 31 Dec, plus 24 Dec which is a US holiday).
- **1 Jan 2027 (Thu) – 4 Jan 2027 (Mon)** — the first 3 business days of the new quarter (1, 4, 5 Jan; 2–3 Jan are the weekend).

So the entire 28 Dec – 4 Jan span sits inside the fiscal-close blackout.

Two important caveats:

1. **It only blocks requests of 3 or more consecutive days.** Your span is 8 days, so a PTO request for it would be "generally denied" under the blackout rule (POL-PTO-001 §4).
2. **An exception is possible with VP-level approval.** Blackout exceptions require VP sign-off (POL-PTO-001 §4). The blackout does not apply to statutory leave, bereavement leave, or jury duty.

If you'd like, tell me which employee this is for and I can run a full compliance check and, if needed, draft a ticket for VP approval.

- (POL-EQUIP-001 §4.1 Stipend): "Remote and hybrid employees receive a one-time home-office stipend of $750 on hire..."
- (POL-BEN-001 §8 Stipends): "Home office | $750 | One-time on hire | Furniture and ergonomics; see `POL-EQUIP-001`"

The stipend covers desks, chairs, lighting, and ergonomic accessories, and is claimed through the expense system. Computing equipment is not covered by the stipend and is purchased directly by IT.
